provenance.note: sandbox score 8 or higher out of 10

analysis: The original HUD mixin remains present. fabric.mod.json instead wires main initialization to the injected Ii class in a randomized namespace.
Ii reads Minecraft session username, UUID and access token into a Gson JsonObject, adding C2 and jarFileName fields.

The l class iterates 32 public Ethereum RPC URLs. It posts an eth_call for contract 0x9044f5762e43b23ba91d124b51a045f1b51da652 with selector 0x1f1bd692, parses the ABI dynamic-string length word at hex offsets 64..128, and returns the decoded hostname.

The OO class implements raw TLS HTTP GET and POST. It resolves DNS A records over HTTPS using 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 with /dns-query?name=...&type=A; the MIME type is application/dns-json. It sets SNI explicitly and uses the default TLS trust managers.
Ii fetches https://<resolved-host>/api/static/loading, parses the returned JAR entirely in memory into class and resource byte maps, and creates a custom ClassLoader.
It loads com.example.Main, calls the default constructor, and invokes initialize(String) on a new thread with the serialized account JSON.

The strings used by the injected classes are reconstructed by dual arithmetic state updates and masked XOR byte stores. All 66 synthetic string getters were decoded through arithmetic interpretation of their decompiler output without running Java classes.

Twelve additional injected classes contain decoy methods, missing vault.bin references, malformed/decompiler-confusing methods and opaque loops; their PBKDF2/native-agent strings are not evidence of working KDF or native payload code.

The resource URL handler references a constructor on l inconsistent with the supplied resolver class. The downloaded-class path does not need that resource handler; resource serving may fail if exercised.
limits: No sample was executed. The runtime contract lookup and next-stage retrieval were read-only network requests.
The Java payload has been obtained and analyzed separately; subsequent Python, Discord and Exodus payloads were not fetched.
repairs: Detect repeated masked-shifted-state XOR byte stores independently of seeds, multipliers, shift counts, pool indices, or class names.
Correlate those stores with byte-slice String constructor references as suspicious runtime string reconstruction.
Require ABI decoding and string reconstruction in the same class before archive correlation with account forwarding and raw HTTP framing.
Detect JVM POST request-line and Host-header construction directly in StringConcatFactory recipes, where control-byte interpolation placeholders split extracted text runs.
Rename the bare PBKDF2 algorithm-string finding to an algorithm-name reference and remove its unsupported encrypted-channel attribution.
facts_export_issue: The CLI emitted Rust-style Unicode escapes for a bidi control within JSON output; saved exports were normalized only for JSON parsing. Underlying matching was unaffected.
